newsitem.title: LATVIA: Pier at Latvia's Ventspils needs months to repair.
newsitem.headline: Pier at Latvia's Ventspils needs months to repair.

text.p: One of the piers at the Ventpils oil terminal will take around four to five months to repair after a tanker crashed into it, company officials said on Wednesday.
They said that at the moment they would not accept vessels longer than 106 metres and said that a 162-metre tanker which has been waiting three days to dock will not be able to dock.

The company which runs the pier, Ventbunkers, said engineers and insurance were currently assessing the damage and it would decide on Thursday the length of vessels it will be able to accept during repairs.

"Work on the pier repair will be very difficult and it might take us as long as four to five months but we will still be able to accept ships," Imants Ozolinsh, Ventbunkers executive director told Reuters.
Norwegian tanker Progress crashed into the pier due to an engine failure on March 27.
"We are for the time being able to accept 106 metres long ships but this is not the final figure yet," Ozolinsh added.
He said the 162-metre tanker owned by the Latvian Shipping company, the Konstantin Cialkovskii, would not be able to dock at the pier.
It has been waiting for three days to load 9,500 tonnes of LUKoil petrol.
